title_en: Law of the People's Republic of China on Mediation and Arbitration of Labor Disputes

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purpose of resolving labor disputes fairly and promptly, protecting the lawful rights and interests of the parties, and promoting harmonious and stable labor relations.

Article 3 In resolving labor disputes, facts shall be taken as the basis, the principles of lawfulness, fairness, timeliness, and emphasis on mediation shall be followed, and the lawful rights and interests of the parties shall be protected according to law.

Article 4 In the event of a labor dispute, the worker may negotiate with the employer, or may request the trade union or a third party to jointly negotiate with the employer to reach a settlement agreement.

Article 5 In the event of a labor dispute, if the parties are unwilling to negotiate, or negotiation fails, or the settlement agreement is not performed after it is reached, they may apply to a mediation organization for mediation; if they are unwilling to mediate, or mediation fails, or the mediation agreement is not performed after it is reached, they may apply to a labor dispute arbitration commission for arbitration; if they refuse to accept the arbitration award, they may file a lawsuit with a People's Court, except as otherwise provided by this Law.

Article 6 In the event of a labor dispute, the parties shall have the responsibility to provide evidence for their own claims. If evidence relating to the disputed matter is under the control and management of the employer, the employer shall provide it; if the employer fails to provide it, the employer shall bear adverse consequences.

Article 7 If there are ten or more workers on one side in a labor dispute and they have common claims, they may elect representatives to participate in mediation, arbitration, or litigation activities.

Article 8 The labor administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level shall, together with the trade union and representatives of the employer side, establish a tripartite mechanism for coordinating labor relations to jointly study and resolve major issues concerning labor disputes.

Article 9 If an employer, in violation of state regulations, delays or fails to pay in full labor remuneration, or delays payment of work-related injury medical expenses, economic compensation, or damages, the worker may complain to the labor administrative department, and the labor administrative department shall handle it according to law.

Article 10 In the event of a labor dispute, the parties may apply for mediation to the following mediation organizations:
(1) the enterprise labor dispute mediation committee;
(2) a grassroots people's mediation organization established according to law; and
(3) an organization established in a township or sub-district that has the function of mediating labor disputes.
An enterprise labor dispute mediation committee shall be composed of worker representatives and employer representatives. The worker representatives shall be held by members of the trade union or elected by all workers, and the employer representatives shall be designated by the responsible person of the enterprise. The director of the enterprise labor dispute mediation committee shall be held by a member of the trade union or a person jointly nominated by both parties.

Article 11 Mediators of labor dispute mediation organizations shall be adult citizens who are fair and upright, maintain close ties with the masses, are enthusiastic about mediation work, and have certain legal knowledge, policy awareness, and cultural level.

Article 12 A party may apply for labor dispute mediation in writing or orally. If the application is made orally, the mediation organization shall record on the spot the basic information of the applicant, the disputed matters for which mediation is sought, the reasons, and the time.
Article 13 In mediating a labor dispute, the mediator shall fully listen to the statements of both parties regarding the facts and reasons, patiently guide them, and help them reach an agreement.

Article 14 If an agreement is reached through mediation, a mediation agreement shall be produced.
The mediation agreement shall be signed or sealed by both parties and shall take effect after being signed by the mediator and sealed with the seal of the mediation organization. It shall be binding on both parties, and the parties shall perform it.
If no mediation agreement is reached within fifteen days from the date on which the labor dispute mediation organization receives the mediation application, the parties may apply for arbitration according to law.
Article 15 After a mediation agreement is reached, if one party fails to perform the mediation agreement within the period agreed upon, the other party may apply for arbitration according to law.

Article 16 If a mediation agreement is reached on matters concerning payment of delayed labor remuneration, work-related injury medical expenses, economic compensation, or damages, and the employer fails to perform it within the period agreed upon, the worker may, holding the mediation agreement, apply to the People's Court for a payment order according to law. The People's Court shall issue a payment order according to law.

Article 17 Labor dispute arbitration commissions shall be established in accordance with the principles of unified planning, rational distribution, and meeting actual needs. The people's government of a province or autonomous region may decide to establish them in cities and counties; the people's government of a municipality directly under the Central Government may decide to establish them in districts and counties. A municipality directly under the Central Government or a city with districts may also establish one or several labor dispute arbitration commissions. Labor dispute arbitration commissions shall not be established at each level of administrative divisions.

Article 18 The labor administrative department of the State Council shall formulate arbitration rules in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law. The labor administrative departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall provide guidance on the labor dispute arbitration work within their respective administrative regions.

Article 19 A labor dispute arbitration commission shall be composed of representatives of the labor administrative department, representatives of the trade union, and representatives of the employer side. The number of members of a labor dispute arbitration commission shall be an odd number.
A labor dispute arbitration commission shall perform the following duties according to law:
(1) appointing and dismissing full-time or part-time arbitrators;
(2) accepting labor dispute cases;
(3) discussing major or difficult labor dispute cases; and
(4) supervising arbitration activities.
A labor dispute arbitration commission shall have an office to handle its daily work.

Article 21 A labor dispute arbitration commission shall have jurisdiction over labor disputes occurring within its region.
A labor dispute shall be under the jurisdiction of the labor dispute arbitration commission at the place of performance of the labor contract or at the place where the employer is located. If both parties apply for arbitration separately to the labor dispute arbitration commission at the place of performance of the labor contract and at the place where the employer is located, the labor dispute arbitration commission at the place of performance of the labor contract shall have jurisdiction.

Article 22 The worker and the employer involved in a labor dispute shall be the two parties in a labor dispute arbitration case.
If a labor dispatch unit or the accepting unit has a labor dispute with a worker, the labor dispatch unit and the accepting unit shall be joint parties.

Article 23 A third party that has an interest in the outcome of the handling of a labor dispute case may apply to participate in arbitration proceedings, or the labor dispute arbitration commission shall notify it to participate in arbitration proceedings.

Article 24 A party may authorize an agent to participate in arbitration proceedings. To authorize another person to participate in arbitration proceedings, a power of attorney signed or sealed by the principal shall be submitted to the labor dispute arbitration commission, and the power of attorney shall specify the matters and scope of authorization.

Article 25 A worker who has lost or partially lost capacity for civil conduct shall be represented by his legal representative in participating in arbitration proceedings; if there is no legal representative, the labor dispute arbitration commission shall designate an agent for him. If the worker is deceased, his close relatives or agents shall participate in arbitration proceedings.
Article 26 Labor dispute arbitration shall be conducted openly, except where the parties agree not to conduct it openly or where state secrets, trade secrets, or personal privacy are involved.

Article 27 The limitation period for applying for arbitration of a labor dispute shall be one year. The limitation period for arbitration shall be calculated from the date on which the party knows or ought to have known that his rights have been infringed.
The arbitration limitation period provided in the preceding paragraph shall be interrupted if one party claims its rights against the other party, or requests rights relief from a relevant department, or the other party agrees to perform its obligations. The limitation period for arbitration shall be recalculated from the time of interruption.
If a party cannot apply for arbitration within the arbitration limitation period provided in the first paragraph of this Article due to force majeure or other legitimate reasons, the arbitration limitation period shall be suspended. The limitation period for arbitration shall continue to run from the date on which the cause for suspension is eliminated.
If a dispute arises from delayed payment of labor remuneration during the existence of the labor relationship, the worker's application for arbitration shall not be subject to the restriction of the arbitration limitation period provided in the first paragraph of this Article; however, if the labor relationship is terminated, the application shall be filed within one year from the date of termination of the labor relationship.

Article 28 An applicant shall submit a written application for arbitration and submit copies thereof according to the number of respondents.
The arbitration application shall specify the following matters:
(1) the name, gender, age, occupation, work unit, and domicile of the worker; the name, domicile, and name and position of the legal representative or principal responsible person of the employer;
(2) the arbitration claims and the facts and reasons on which they are based; and
(3) the evidence and the source of the evidence, and the names and domiciles of witnesses.
If it is truly difficult to write an arbitration application, an oral application may be made, and the labor dispute arbitration commission shall record it in the written record and inform the other party.

Article 29 Within five days from the date of receipt of an arbitration application, the labor dispute arbitration commission shall, if it deems that the application meets the acceptance conditions, accept the case and notify the applicant; if it deems that the application does not meet the acceptance conditions, it shall notify the applicant in writing of the rejection and state the reasons. If the labor dispute arbitration commission rejects the case or fails to make a decision within the time limit, the applicant may file a lawsuit with the People's Court regarding the labor dispute matter.

Article 30 After accepting an arbitration application, the labor dispute arbitration commission shall serve a copy of the arbitration application on the respondent within five days.
After receiving the copy of the arbitration application, the respondent shall submit a statement of defense to the labor dispute arbitration commission within ten days. After receiving the statement of defense, the labor dispute arbitration commission shall serve a copy thereof on the applicant within five days. The failure of the respondent to submit a statement of defense shall not affect the conduct of the arbitration proceedings.

Article 31 A labor dispute arbitration commission shall adopt the arbitration tribunal system for adjudicating labor dispute cases. An arbitration tribunal shall be composed of three arbitrators, with a chief arbitrator. A simple labor dispute case may be arbitrated by a single arbitrator alone.

Article 32 The labor dispute arbitration commission shall notify the parties in writing of the composition of the arbitration tribunal within five days from the date of acceptance of the arbitration application.

Article 34 If an arbitrator falls under the circumstance specified in Item (4) of Article 33 of this Law, or commits acts of soliciting or accepting bribes, engaging in malpractice for personal gain, or perverting the law in making an award, he shall bear legal liability according to law. The labor dispute arbitration commission shall dismiss him.

Article 35 The arbitration tribunal shall notify both parties in writing of the date and place of the hearing five days before the hearing. If a party has legitimate reasons, it may request a postponement of the hearing three days before the hearing. Whether to postpone the hearing shall be decided by the labor dispute arbitration commission.

Article 36 If the applicant, after receiving written notice, fails to appear in court without legitimate reasons or withdraws from the hearing without the consent of the arbitration tribunal, the application may be deemed as withdrawn.
If the respondent, after receiving written notice, fails to appear in court without legitimate reasons or withdraws from the hearing without the consent of the arbitration tribunal, an award may be made by default.

Article 37 If the arbitration tribunal considers that an expert evaluation is necessary for a specialized issue, it may submit the matter for evaluation to an expert evaluation institution agreed upon by the parties; if the parties have not agreed or cannot reach an agreement, it shall be evaluated by an expert evaluation institution designated by the arbitration tribunal.
Upon the request of a party or at the request of the arbitration tribunal, the expert evaluation institution shall send its expert evaluator to attend the hearing. With the permission of the arbitration tribunal, the parties may question the expert evaluator.

Article 38 During the arbitration proceedings, the parties shall have the right to cross-examine evidence and to debate. At the conclusion of cross-examination and debate, the chief arbitrator or the sole arbitrator shall solicit the final opinions of the parties.

Article 39 If evidence provided by a party is verified as true, the arbitration tribunal shall take it as the basis for determining the facts.
If a worker cannot provide evidence that is under the control and management of the employer and relates to the arbitration claims, the arbitration tribunal may require the employer to provide it within a specified period. If the employer fails to provide it within the specified period, the employer shall bear adverse consequences.

Article 40 The arbitration tribunal shall keep a written record of the hearing. If a party or any other participant in the arbitration considers that there are omissions or errors in the record of their statements, they have the right to apply for corrections. If corrections are not made, the application shall be recorded.
The written record shall be signed or sealed by the arbitrator, the recorder, the parties, and other participants in the arbitration.
Article 41 After applying for labor dispute arbitration, the parties may settle the matter by themselves. If a settlement agreement is reached, they may withdraw the arbitration application.

Article 42 Before making an award, the arbitration tribunal shall first conduct mediation.
If an agreement is reached through mediation, the arbitration tribunal shall produce a mediation document.
The mediation document shall state the arbitration claims and the result of the agreement between the parties. The mediation document shall be signed by the arbitrator, sealed with the seal of the labor dispute arbitration commission, and served on both parties. The mediation document shall take legal effect after being signed for by both parties.
If mediation fails or if a party repudiates before the mediation document is served, the arbitration tribunal shall promptly make an award.

Article 43 An arbitration tribunal shall conclude the adjudication of a labor dispute case within forty-five days from the date on which the labor dispute arbitration commission accepts the arbitration application. If the case is complex and requires an extension, with the approval of the director of the labor dispute arbitration commission, the period may be extended and the parties shall be notified in writing; however, the extended period shall not exceed fifteen days. If no arbitration award is made within the time limit, the parties may file a lawsuit with the People's Court regarding the labor dispute matter.
When an arbitration tribunal adjudicates a labor dispute case, if part of the facts are already clear, it may make an award on that part first.

Article 44 For cases involving claims for labor remuneration, work-related injury medical expenses, economic compensation, or damages, the arbitration tribunal may, upon the application of a party, rule on advance execution and transfer the case to the People's Court for enforcement.
If the arbitration tribunal rules on advance execution, the following conditions shall be met:
(1) the rights and obligations between the parties are clear; and
(2) failure to grant advance execution would seriously affect the livelihood of the applicant.
If a worker applies for advance execution, he may not provide security.

Article 45 An award shall be made in accordance with the opinions of the majority of the arbitrators, and the dissenting opinions of the minority arbitrators shall be recorded in the written record. If the arbitration tribunal cannot form a majority opinion, the award shall be made in accordance with the opinion of the chief arbitrator.

Article 46 An award shall state the arbitration claims, the facts of the dispute, the reasons for the award, the result of the award, and the date of the award. The award shall be signed by the arbitrator(s) and sealed with the seal of the labor dispute arbitration commission. An arbitrator who disagrees with the award may sign or may not sign.

Article 47 For the following labor disputes, except as otherwise provided by this Law, the arbitration award shall be final, and the award shall take legal effect from the date on which it is made:
(1) disputes involving claims for labor remuneration, work-related injury medical expenses, economic compensation, or damages, where the amount does not exceed the local monthly minimum wage standard for twelve months; and
(2) disputes arising from the implementation of national labor standards in respect of working hours, rest and leave, social insurance, and the like.

Article 48 A worker who refuses to accept the arbitration award specified in Article 47 of this Law may file a lawsuit with the People's Court within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the award.

Article 50 A party who refuses to accept an arbitration award in a labor dispute case other than those specified in Article 47 of this Law may file a lawsuit with the People's Court within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the award; if no lawsuit is filed within the time limit, the award shall take legal effect.

Article 51 The parties shall perform mediation documents and awards that have taken legal effect within the prescribed time limit. If one party fails to perform within the time limit, the other party may apply to the People's Court for enforcement in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law. The People's Court that accepts the application shall enforce it according to law.

Article 52 If a staff member of a public institution under the employment system has a labor dispute with the institution, this Law shall apply; if laws, administrative regulations, or the State Council provide otherwise, those provisions shall apply.
Article 53 Labor dispute arbitration shall not charge fees. The funds of the labor dispute arbitration commissions shall be guaranteed by public finance.
Article 54 This Law shall come into force as of May 1, 2008.
